speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: asked Minister for Education (a) how are parents and care-givers of students in Special Education (SPED) schools and students with special educational needs (SEN) supported with home-based learning during the circuit breaker period; (b) whether students who need regular therapy sessions are able to attend the sessions; and (c) what efforts are put in place to ensure that these students do not regress during this period.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The packages included both online and offline learning materials.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Offline learning is an important part of HBL, especially for students in SPED schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Teachers adjusted their materials and pedagogy to engage the students online and accommodate their learning needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For instance, some use recorded instructions and "live" lessons to help students with reading difficulties.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: SPED teachers prepared customised lesson packages with high levels of interactive, visual and concrete supports.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For students with sensory or physical challenges, schools have ensured continued access to needed assistive technology and communication devices.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This includes the loan of customised devices and tools to support students' learning at home.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Teachers and other school personnel check in regularly with the students or through their parents to monitor their well-being and learning progress.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For students with ASD, schools share strategies and resources with parents, including social stories to help them cope with the changes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: SPED School Allied Professionals such as psychologists, occupational therapists, speech and language therapists and physiotherapists also work with teachers to integrate interventions into lesson plans or share these with parents through video or teleconferencing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: A small group of students with very high support needs and assessed by the schools to need school-based interventions have been invited to come back to school for limited services, with the necessary safe-distancing precautions in place.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Hence, therapy services can continue, but with safe distancing precautions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These include keeping therapy one-to-one, and prioritising face-to-face consultations for patients whose condition may significantly or rapidly deteriorate otherwise.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In other cases, providers are encouraged to deliver their outpatient services by tele-consultation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We understand that full HBL can be challenging for parents and care-givers of children with SEN, especially if they have to work from home or have other children who are also on HBL.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They should feel free to reach out to their child's school for guidance, help and support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They can also tap other sources of assistance, such as the National Care Helpline, that various Government and Social Service Agencies are offering.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MOE, MOH and MSF will reflect on these findings carefully and use them to inform our efforts to support you and your children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One thing that comes across in the survey is how critical it is for children with SEN to spend some time outdoors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is necessary for self-regulation, especially for children with ASD and ADHD.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I call on everyone to be more understanding when they see a parent with a child with SEN in a park or public space getting a bit of fresh air.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Sometimes, the children – and they could be adult children – will not be wearing a mask.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government understands and has stated that enforcement will be flexible for such persons.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, give those families a smile and a friendly wave to show that you understand.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It is indeed heartening to note that specific efforts have been put in place to support parents.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I think that you rightly pointed out, it is a challenging journey, especially for the parents; it can be quite frustrating because it is not easy.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: With the teachers' help, it actually facilitates a lot of the training for the kids when they are in schools, but at home doing it on their own, it can be a bit challenging.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: So, I am glad to know that there is support through teleconferencing, teleconsultation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Given the circumstances, especially as you highlighted, for some of those children with special needs, the fact that they now have to limit their time outdoors or to limit their interactions with other peers, these all have an effect on their development.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: So, I am wondering whether the school, looking at various safe distancing measures and how we can support this, could also look at how we can have more of sessions physically aside from just leaving it to the parents.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I know that you have a few students who are actually going to the schools to receive therapies but these are for the more serious cases.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am just wondering for the regular cases, whether you could also consider having sessions where parents and the students could come to school and have regular interactions, because I think that would matter.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But the teachers also made great effort to do exercise sessions online.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I know this because I participated in one of them, and I have to say that the workout was not a light workout, you could work up quite a sweat.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You could see that the teachers prepared the exercises beforehand.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They made sure that the children were paying attention and following online.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is not the same, obviously, as when they are in school, they can see their friends face-to-face and they interact with the teachers directly, but the schools have made an effort to ensure that the children do continue to have physical exercise during home-based learning (HBL).

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It helps them to feel safe and to follow a regular structure.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But I do take on board the Member's point about how we can look for other ways to facilitate interaction.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And also that suggestion of teleconferencing and how it can be done better.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We will take them on board, see how we can refine them to make sure that we have a good process, going forward.
